(견고한 재무구조를 가진 기업이 선호됩니다.) Market # The market finished today on a decidedly uneven note, but the prevailing mood remains one of guarded optimism. Equities didn’t surge, nor did they retreat with panicked selling. Instead, we saw a continuation of the trend that has been building for months: a steady shift from growth to value. (지정학적 긴장이 유가를 끌어올렸습니다.) news as well—a sign that markets are focused on fundamentals rather than fleeting crises. The bottom line Today's Voca bottom line[ˈbɑː.təm laɪn]Cost cuts helped protect the bottom line. (비용 절감이 순이익을 방어하는 데 도움이 됐습니다.) is, despite the noise, the market has shown a remarkable ability to lift itself and shrug off setbacks.
The biggest news of the day involved two massive deals: Paramount’s merger with Warner Bros. gaining DOJ approval, and SpaceX’s blockbuster Today's Voca blockbuster[ˈblɑːk.bʌs.tər]A blockbuster quarter sent the stock to record highs. (대박 분기 실적이 주가를 사상 최고치로 보냈습니다.) IPO. Let’s unpack those and the other key trends bubbling beneath the surface.
Key Stories # SpaceX Soars, But Tesla Echoes – A Lesson in IPO Valuation Today's Voca Valuation[ˌvæl.juˈeɪ.ʃən]Tech valuations look stretched after the rally. (랠리 이후 기술주 밸류에이션이 과열된 것으로 보입니다.) The SpaceX IPO was, as Musk himself said, “not sure that this could have gone much better.” A $75 billion raise is a staggering sum, and the speed and success of the offering underscore the insatiable appetite for disruptive technologies, even at a premium. But the comparison to Tesla’s initial performance – looking at both the one-day pop and the five-year return – is a cautionary tale. SpaceX’s future is predicated on continued innovation and expansion into space exploration and commercialization. Tesla’s story, while undeniably compelling, has been punctuated by significant volatility and management challenges. Investors need to ask themselves: are they buying into a narrative or a demonstrated business model? While the SpaceX IPO is undeniably exciting, it carries the same risks of high valuation and future uncertainty that have plagued other hyped-up growth stocks. It’s a moment to buy the dip Today's Voca buy the dip[baɪ ðə dɪp]Retail investors bought the dip in mega-cap tech. (개인 투자자들이 초대형 기술주 조정 구간을 매수했습니다.) on existing positions, and to be selective about any new allocations.
Value’s Reign: Growth is Yesterday’s Story
The outperformance of value stocks versus growth equities continues to be a compelling narrative. This isn’t a flash in the pan, as many are now acknowledging. Investors are clearly prioritizing companies with solid balance sheets, proven earnings, and reasonable valuations, eschewing the speculative Today's Voca speculative[ˈspek.jə.lə.tɪv]Speculative trades faded as rates moved higher. (금리 상승에 투기적 거래가 줄었습니다.) fervor that characterized much of the last decade. This trend is data-dependent Today's Voca data-dependent[ˈdeɪ.tə dɪˈpen.dənt]The Fed stressed a data-dependent approach. (연준은 데이터 의존적 접근을 강조했습니다.) . As long as the economy remains reasonably sturdy—and the Federal Reserve Today's Voca Federal Reserve[ˈfed.ər.əl rɪˈzɜːrv]Markets are pricing in another Federal Reserve rate move. (시장은 연준의 추가 금리 조치를 반영하고 있습니다.) offers signals that suggest a dovish pivot—value will continue to catch a bid Today's Voca catch a bid[kætʃ ə bɪd]Treasuries caught a bid as stocks sold off. Geopolitical Tensions and Persian Gulf Oil Flows: A Mixed Bag for Energy
The news concerning Persian Gulf oil flows, bolstered by U.S. escorts, is an interesting development. A seven million barrel-per-day flow rate is substantial, but it’s crucial to remember that global demand is a moving target. While this development eases some concerns about supply disruptions, it doesn’t necessarily translate into a bullish outlook for energy equities. Meanwhile, gold is gaining ground on hopes of a U.S.-Iran deal, potentially tempering expectations of further rate hikes. This illustrates the complex interplay of geopolitical factors and monetary policy Today's Voca monetary policy[məˈnɛt.ər.i ˈpɑː.lə.si]Federal Reserve monetary policy remains in focus. (연준의 통화 정책이 여전히 핵심 관심사입니다.) —a challenge for even the most seasoned investor.
Today’s Takeaway # Don’t mistake a lack of fireworks for a lack of action. The market’s resilience and the ongoing rotation towards value are quietly reshaping the investment landscape. Ignore the noise, build a sturdy portfolio focused on fundamentals, and you might just find yourself pleasantly surprised by year-end. This isn’t about chasing the latest headline; it’s about playing it safe and lock in gains Today's Voca lock in gains[lɑːk ɪn ɡeɪnz]Traders locked in gains after the sharp morning rally. Market Brief: June 12, 2026 · Pre-Market # Market Overview # The market is waking up to a distinctly lighter mood this morning, and rightfully so. Overnight, oil prices tumbled – significantly – on the back of reports suggesting a potential peace deal with Iran could be finalized within days. This, coupled with surprisingly robust consumer sentiment data and the impending debut of SpaceX (which, let’s be honest, everyone’s been waiting for), is creating a tentative, but palpable, relief rally Today's Voca relief rally[rɪˈliːf ˈræ.li]Software names led a relief rally in enterprise tech. (소프트웨어 종목이 기업용 IT 섹터 반등을 이끌었습니다.) . Futures are pointing higher, but we’re operating under a precarious Today's Voca precarious/ˈpriːkəriəs/The combination of rising inflation and increased AI spending creates a precarious situation for the technology sector. (상승하는 인플레이션과 증가하는 AI 관련 지출은 기술 부문에게 불안정한 상황을 만들어 냅니다.) equilibrium Today's Voca equilibrium[ˌiːkwɪˈlɪbriəm]The market is operating under a precarious equilibrium following the oil price drop. (유가 하락 이후 시장은 불안정한 균형 상태를 유지하고 있습니다.) . The air feels charged with anticipation, but also a lingering caution – a sense that the easy gains may be behind us.
The SpaceX IPO is, undeniably, the story everyone is talking about. It’s a testament to the resilient Today's Voca resilient[rɪˈzɪl.jənt]Investors favor companies with resilient balance sheets. (견고한 재무구조를 가진 기업이 선호됩니다.) nature of private capital markets, and the enduring allure of disruptive technology. However, the hype is bordering on feverish, and investors need to tread carefully, remembering the lessons of past IPO frenzies. This isn’t just about the potential upside of SpaceX; it’s a bellwether Today's Voca bellwether[ˈbel.wɛð.ər]FedEx is seen as a bellwether for global trade. (FedEx는 글로벌 무역의 선행 지표로 여겨집니다.) for the broader IPO market, signaling a possible reopening of the capital markets. JPMorgan’s call on Goldman and Morgan Stanley is worth noting, too - a big IPO pipeline should be a strong tailwind for the big banks.
Yet, the oil price drop is the macro theme that truly move the needle Today's Voca move the needle[muːv ðə ˈniː.dəl]The CPI print failed to move the needle for the Fed. (CPI 발표는 연준의 방향을 바꾸지 못했습니다.) today. Lower oil prices are a positive for the consumer – a welcome respite from persistent inflation – but they also pose a risk to energy producers and, potentially, wider global economic growth. The Iran deal itself, while a potential geopolitical Today's Voca geopolitical[ˌdʒi.oʊ.pəˈlɪt.ɪ.kəl]Geopolitical tensions pushed oil prices higher. (지정학적 긴장이 유가를 끌어올렸습니다.) win, introduces its own set of uncertainties and could trigger renewed tensions elsewhere. We’re seeing a confluence Today's Voca confluence/kənˈfluːəns/The market's recent volatility was a confluence of concerns, including inflation and geopolitical tensions. (시장의 최근 변동성은 인플레이션과 지정학적 긴장 등 여러 우려 요인이 한꺼번에 발생한 결과였습니다.) of forces – hope, anxiety, and the ever-present specter of inflation – all vying for attention.
Key Stories # Iran Deal & Oil Prices: The overnight drop in oil prices is the biggest story, without question. The prospect of increased Iranian oil supply has immediately knocked down crude inventories, catching those who were long in oil off guard. Bank of America’s advice to investors to buy the dip Today's Voca buy the dip[baɪ ðə dɪp]Retail investors bought the dip in mega-cap tech. (개인 투자자들이 초대형 기술주 조정 구간을 매수했습니다.) is a reasonable reaction, particularly for those with a long-term horizon, but we’re not calling a full reversal. This is a relief rally, and the potential for a renewed leg higher remains contingent on the deal’s final terms and its impact on broader geopolitical stability. Don’t be surprised to see some profit-taking as the reality of the situation settles in. The lingering question remains: is this a sustainable headwind for inflation, or a precursor to something more complex?
SpaceX’s Record IPO: The buzz surrounding SpaceX’s IPO is almost deafening. The sheer scale of the offering, combined with Elon Musk’s personal brand, is generating massive FOMO (Fear of Missing Out). The investor commentary about its potential pivot to Nvidia, and the wider implications for AI infrastructure, are definitely worth paying attention to. However, it’s crucial to remember the cautionary tales of overhyped IPOs past. As one investor rightly pointed out, a dip isn’t a blip for retirees. The stock will likely catch a bid Today's Voca catch a bid[kætʃ ə bɪd]Treasuries caught a bid as stocks sold off. (주식 매도세에 국채가 매수세를 받았습니다.) today, but the real test will be its performance in the coming weeks and months. Focus on corporate governance Today's Voca corporate governance[ˈɡʌv.ər.nəns]IPO investors scrutinized corporate governance structures. (IPO 투자자들은 기업 지배구조를 면밀히 검토했습니다.) and the long-term sustainability of SpaceX’s business model, rather than getting caught up in the short-term frenzy.
Consumer Sentiment & Inflation: The upward tick in consumer sentiment, driven primarily by easing gasoline prices, provides further support for the risk-on sentiment. It suggests consumers are feeling slightly more confident about the economic outlook, despite persistent inflationary pressures Today's Voca inflationary pressures[ɪnˈfleɪ.ʃən.er.i]Oil spikes added fresh inflationary pressures. (유가 급등이 새로운 인플레이션 압력을 더했습니다.) . This is a welcome sign, particularly as we approach the critical jobs report Today's Voca jobs report[dʒɑːbz rɪˈpɔːrt]A strong jobs report revived rate-hike expectations. (견고한 고용 보고서가 금리 인상 기대를 되살렸습니다.) later this month. It’s a small step in what might be an inflection point Today's Voca inflection point[ɪnˈflɛkʃən pɔɪnt]The sudden drop in tech stocks marked an inflection point, suggesting a potential shift in the market's trajectory. (주식 시장의 기술주 급락은 시장의 잠재적 전환점을 나타내는 징후입니다.) for the US consumer, but it’s not a declaration of victory on the inflation front.
Today’s Takeaway # Don’t be lulled into a false sense of security by today’s rally. The Iran deal, while positive in the short term, introduces new geopolitical risks, and the SpaceX IPO, while exciting, is a high-stakes gamble. Be selective, play it safe Today's Voca play it safe[pleɪ ɪt seɪf]Fund managers played it safe into month-end. (펀드 매니저들은 월말을 앞두고 안전하게 운용했습니다.) with a portion of your portfolio, and remember that even the most resilient markets can tumble unexpectedly. This isn’t a signal to abandon caution – it’s a reminder to navigate the market with a clear head and a long-term perspective.

Market Brief: June 12, 2026 · After the Close # The Age of Uncertainty: A Market Weighing Demographics, Geopolitics, and AI’s Unpredictability # Today’s market felt decidedly cautious. The Dow closed down 0.8%, the S&P 500 retreated 0.9%, and the Nasdaq fared slightly worse, shedding 1.2%. This isn’t a panic; more a collective sigh of apprehension as investors grapple with a confluence Today's Voca confluence/kənˈfluːəns/The market's recent volatility was a confluence of concerns, including inflation and geopolitical tensions. (시장의 최근 변동성은 인플레이션과 지정학적 긴장 등 여러 우려 요인이 한꺼번에 발생한 결과였습니다.) of headwinds. The underlying theme of the session: the future is murky, and the market is taking no chances. Fixed-income Today's Voca Fixed-income[fɪkst ˈɪn.kʌm]Bond turmoil created a challenging fixed-income environment. (채권 혼란이 채권 시장 환경을 어렵게 만들었습니다.) markets offered little buoyancy, and the bid-ask spread Today's Voca bid-ask spread[bɪd æsk spred]Wider bid-ask spreads signaled thinner liquidity. (매수·매도 호가 스프레드 확대는 유동성 감소를 시사했습니다.) remained stubbornly wide—a sure sign of hesitant participation.
The macro picture is undeniably contributing to the unease. The headlines surrounding Social Security insolvency Today's Voca insolvency[ɪnˈsɒlvənsi]The possibility of government insolvency is weighing heavily on consumer confidence. (정부의 지급 불능 가능성은 소비자 신뢰에 큰 영향을 미치고 있다.) —while presenting a “simple” solution—highlight a political gridlock that’s unlikely to resolve itself anytime soon. This casts a long shadow over consumer spending, especially among the older demographic who represent a significant portion of the market. Then there’s the persistent specter of trade tensions Today's Voca trade tensions[ˈtɛn.ʃənz]Trade tensions with China remain a summer risk. (중국과의 무역 긴장은 여전히 하계 리스크입니다.) . Shell’s agreements with Venezuela, coupled with the U.S. overtaking Saudi Arabia and Russia as the world’s top oil exporter, underscore the shifting global power dynamics—and the potential for unpredictable disruptions. The market is trying to read the tea leaves Today's Voca read the tea leaves[riːd ðə tiː liːvz]Investors read the tea leaves from Fed speakers. (투자자들은 연준 인사 발언에서 단서를 읽었습니다.) , and the picture isn’t clear.
But the biggest story, and perhaps the most important to understand the market’s current state of mind, is the narrative around technology—specifically, the AI boom and its potential downsides. The Adobe woes—another top executive departing—are a stark reminder that even the seemingly unstoppable growth stories can stumble. The AI-driven World Cup predictions, picking underdogs based on algorithms, offer a quirky metaphor for the market’s own attempts to forecast the future, reminding us that even sophisticated models can be wrong.
Key Stories
Adobe’s Troubles Continue: The ongoing executive exodus at Adobe is creating a drag on sentiment, and the stock’s continued slide below $400—hitting a seven-year low—is unsettling. While some argue this is an opportunity to buy the dip Today's Voca buy the dip[baɪ ðə dɪp]Retail investors bought the dip in mega-cap tech. (개인 투자자들이 초대형 기술주 조정 구간을 매수했습니다.) , the market is clearly concerned about the company’s strategic direction and execution. The real story is that this isn’t just about Adobe. It’s a reminder that the frothy valuations of many tech companies, inflated by AI hype, may be due for a paring back. Investors need to scrutinize recurring revenue Today's Voca recurring revenue[rɪˈkɜːr.ɪŋ ˈrev.ən.juː]Recurring revenue now accounts for 70% of sales. (반복 매출이 전체 매출의 70%를 차지합니다.) and genuine product innovation—not just speculative Today's Voca speculative[ˈspek.jə.lə.tɪv]Speculative trades faded as rates moved higher. (금리 상승에 투기적 거래가 줄었습니다.) buzz—to discern which companies can truly justify their valuations.
U.S. Energy Ascendancy: The United States’ surge to become the top oil exporter is a geopolitical Today's Voca geopolitical[ˌdʒi.oʊ.pəˈlɪt.ɪ.kəl]Geopolitical tensions pushed oil prices higher. (지정학적 긴장이 유가를 끌어올렸습니다.) game-changer. It’s a clear reflection of the energy revolution spurred by fracking and technological advancements. This development could offset some of the inflationary pressure from rising oil prices, but it also creates new avenues for trade tensions and potential conflicts of interest. The move is priced in to some degree—the market has been anticipating this shift—but the ramifications for OPEC+ and global energy markets are just beginning to unfold. We should watch the capital expenditure Today's Voca capital expenditure[ˈkæp.ɪ.təl ɪkˈspend.ɪ.tʃər]Big Tech faces rising capital expenditure for AI buildouts. (빅테크는 AI 구축을 위해 자본 지출 부담이 커지고 있습니다.) plans of U.S. energy companies carefully; aggressive investment could further bolster production and depress prices.
The Golden Age of LNG: Venture Global and Greece’s Atlantic-SEE doubling their U.S. LNG supply deal is indicative of a broader trend: Europe’s desperate search for alternative energy sources. Investors are reportedly raising cash in anticipation of the offering, leading to downward pressure on existing tech stocks. The situation highlights the potential for individual events, even those as momentous as a SpaceX IPO, to exert significant influence on market trends. The market is particularly sensitive to cash flows related to large IPOs like SpaceX’s, given the current cautious environment.

The move suggests concerns about Nike’s ability to capitalize on the event’s potential boost to sales, possibly reflecting broader concerns about consumer spending and the company’s competitive position. While the World Cup typically drives increased sportswear demand, RBC’s downgrade suggests that the anticipated benefit may not materialize to the extent previously expected.
3. Today’s Takeaway
Investor caution remains paramount. While the market has stabilized somewhat following the CPI data, the underlying conditions – including lingering inflation concerns, geopolitical risks, and the potential for a correction fueled by exuberant sentiment – demand a measured approach. The SpaceX IPO serves as a potent reminder that individual events can significantly impact market sentiment Today's Voca market sentiment[ˈsen.tɪ.mənt]Market sentiment turned cautious after the jobs report. About Stock Agent News # Stock Agent News is a fully automated AI-powered stock market analysis platform. Twice daily ( 07:00 and 21:30 KST ), the system collects news, writes an English market brief in an opinion-column voice, attaches a cover image and optional audio, and publishes to GitHub Pages — with no manual editing step.
How It Works # Data collection — RSS feeds from three sources (~25–30 articles per run). AI analysis — A local LLM (Ollama + Gemma 3 12B QAT) synthesizes a narrative, analytical market brief (~1,000–1,500 words) with a clear point of view. Cover image — A random thumbnail from an article that includes an image (RSS media fields or article page); saved with source attribution. Audio brief — Piper TTS (local ONNX) reads the English brief aloud; one WAV per session with an in-page player (~15 sec to generate on M1). Gemini TTS remains available as a fallback via config. Earnings calendar — yfinance scans all S&P 500 tickers on Yahoo Finance for the next 7 days; listed after Today’s Takeaway with quote, estimates, and company links. Vocabulary tooltips — Key finance terms are wrapped with the Hugo voca shortcode (pronunciation + bilingual example). Desktop: hover; mobile: tap. Smart positioning anchors the popup above or below the word, shifts it away from screen edges, and raises z-index so headings do not bleed through. The dictionary ( 330+ terms — nouns, verbs, adjectives, Wall Street idioms) grows daily via Ollama suggest + auto-review (2e_vocab_suggest.py), including inflected forms (eschewing → eschew). Deploy — Hugo builds the static site and pushes to GitHub Pages. The public endpoint began returning HTTP 402 when paid Pollen credits became required. The pipeline now uses RSS-sourced images instead — no image-gen API.
S&P 500 earnings (yfinance) # Each daily brief includes an Upcoming S&P 500 Earnings section after Today’s Takeaway. The pipeline scans all ~500 S&P constituents via yfinance (Ticker.calendar) and filters to the next 7 days. Each row links to the Yahoo Finance quote, an earnings estimates page, and the company website when available. Constituents list comes from a public S&P 500 CSV (cached 24 h). No API key required.
Previously FMP was used, but the free tier returned only a handful of rows per request and omitted major names (e.g. Broadcom on dates when it was in-window).

Development log Pipeline and site changes, grouped by month — similar to a release-notes page. New entries are appended after each meaningful update. June 2026 What's new on June 13, 2026 Opinion-style briefs, vocabulary expansion, and post timestamps
Writing & voice
Daily briefs now use an opinion-column voice (Barron’s / Bloomberg Opinion style) — analytical, narrative, with a clear point of view. Each run samples ~24 terms from data/vocabulary.yaml into the LLM prompt (verbs, adjectives, Wall Street idioms). LLM-generated headlines (second Ollama call) with session label — {headline} · Pre-Market / · After the Close. Twice-daily US sessions
Pre-Market (21:30 KST) — before US cash open; After the Close (07:00 KST) — after US close. Separate JSON, Hugo posts, slugs, and audio/image assets per session (daily-brief-pre-market.md, daily-brief-post-market.md). infer_session() fixed — KST before 21:30 → post-market; 21:30+ → pre-market. run_all.sh fixed for macOS bash 3.2 (SESSION_FLAG unbound variable). Vocabulary (330+ terms)
Manual expansion to 330+ entries — nouns, verbs, adjectives, and American/Wall Street idioms (priced in, catch a bid, move the needle, etc.). 2e_vocab_suggest.py now scans the brief for unknown tokens (e.g. eschewing) and prioritizes them for auto-promotion. Inflection matching in voca.py — eschewing matches dictionary entry eschew; -ing/-ed/-s forms supported. Up to 8 new terms promoted per run (was 5); full archive re-annotated with --all. Site
Hugo frontmatter date now includes execution time — e.g. 2026-06-13T07:33:11 (KST). generated_at stored in brief JSON; legacy posts backfilled from file mtime on regenerate. What's new on June 09, 2026 Local Piper TTS and pipeline reliability fixes
Audio briefs (Piper TTS)
Switched default TTS from Gemini to Piper TTS — local ONNX on M1, no API key or billing. Voice: en_US-lessac-medium; ~15 sec to synthesize a full daily brief (~6 min audio). 2c_tts.py supports dual backends — tts.provider: piper or gemini in config.yaml. Gemini TTS skipped gracefully on HTTP 429 (prepay credits depleted). Pipeline fixes
Fixed 1_fetch.py — raw article filenames now use KST (was UTC), matching brief dates. 2b_image.py — fallback to latest raw fetch when date-prefixed file is missing. Site
June 09 daily brief published with Piper-generated audio. What's new on June 07, 2026 Vocabulary tooltips (voca), smart popup UX, and pipeline fixes
Vocabulary tooltips (voca)
New Hugo voca shortcode — hover/focus shows pronunciation (IPA) and bilingual example sentences. Built data/vocabulary.yaml (85 terms) from all daily briefs published to date. Pipeline step 5_generate_content.py auto-wraps up to 15 terms per post (once per term). New step 2e_vocab_suggest.py — Ollama suggests new terms daily, LLM auto-reviews, and promotes approved entries. Rejected candidates logged in data/vocabulary_rejected.yaml. Smart tooltip UX
Word-anchored popup — default below the term; flips above (flip-top) when bottom space is under 180px. Horizontal edge detection — --popup-shift keeps the card inside the viewport; arrow tracks the word. Mobile tap to open; desktop hover; Today’s Voca header on each card. z-index fix — .is-active / :hover elevates the tooltip above Blowfish heading layers (no text bleed-through). Logic in site/assets/js/voca.js; styles in site/assets/css/custom.css. Pipeline fixes
Fixed 2d_earnings.py — yfinance Timestamp vs date comparison bug (earnings section was silently skipped). Strip LLM-generated References block from brief body; RSS-linked References added separately. TTS chunk size lowered to 2,800 chars — fixes mid-audio truncation on long briefs. Site
Tooltip CSS — solid light/dark card backgrounds with .prose override. Full pipeline re-run and deploy for June 07 daily brief. What's new on June 06, 2026 RSS images, Gemini TTS, earnings calendar (yfinance), and AdSense

Retired Pollinations.ai — legacy endpoint returned HTTP 402 (~June 3); generation now requires paid Pollen credits. Cover art picked at random from RSS articles (media_content, summary <img>, or og:image fallback). Saved as site/static/images/YYYY/MM/DD/daily-brief.{ext} with source credit line. Audio briefs (TTS)
New pipeline step 2c_tts.py — Gemini TTS (gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts, voice Kore). Long briefs chunked (~5,000 chars), merged into one WAV per day at /audio/YYYY/MM/DD/daily-brief.wav. Earnings calendar

RSS / og:image covers, yfinance, Ollama (local), GitHub Pages — $0. Gemini TTS — Google AI Studio free tier (~1–2 calls/day). What's new on June 03, 2026 Pollinations outage — RSS image backfill for 6/3–6/5
